title: TaskList/set onDestroyRemoveTasks=true orphans the list's Tasks
description: handle_task_list_set (crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/task_list.rs ~281-310) with onDestroyRemoveTasks=true skips the task_list_has_tasks check and calls only destroy_object::<TaskList>. The module doc (task_list.rs:3-6) says 'If true, the backend destroys the tasks along with the list', but TasksBackend::destroy_object takes no flag and MemoryBackend::destroy_object (src/memory.rs) removes only the TaskList record. Result: Tasks whose taskListId names the destroyed list survive, with no Task state bump or destroyed entry in Task/changes. draft-tasks onDestroyRemoveTasks: if true, tasks in the list are destroyed with it. Siblings drive this cascade in the handler: calendars Calendar/set onDestroyRemoveEvents (calendar.rs ~320) and contacts AddressBook/set onDestroyRemoveContents (cascade_address_book_contents). Fix: mirror that handler-driven cascade (destroy Tasks in the list via destroy_object::<Task>, then the list), fix the module doc, and add a test whose oracle is the draft text. Found during JMAP-x2gd.86 doc sweep.
close_reason: Landed in d7fae941 fix(tasks-server): cascade onDestroyRemoveTasks (batch 5, adversarially verified, CI green at 44026b06)
